title: kate-core: replay a journal onto the text on disk
summary: replay_journal applies the journal lines in order to the text that is on disk and returns the recovered text. A line whose old text does not match the buffer is a Mismatch, and a line whose revision_before is not the previous revision_after is a Revision error. The first line's revision_before is not checked.

lane.reason: A Cursor cloud agent codes this packet. workspace.rs is a 3,500-line file and the change touches its command dispatch. The Linux VM builds and tests kate-core. The owner Mac stays free for the window.

definitions.definition:
/// The text after every line applies to `text`.
pub fn replay_journal(text: &str, lines: &[JournalLine]) -> Result<String, ReplayError>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Build a TextBuffer::from_str(text). For each line build Edits and a Transaction::new; a TransactionError is Overlap. Apply it; ApplyError::OldTextMismatch and OutOfBounds are Mismatch. Return buffer.text().to_string(). ReplayError and replay_journal are pub and carry #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))] until the stash packet exports them. The test replay_applies_the_lines_in_order replays two lines onto ab: insert X at 0 with revisions 0 to 1, then replace b at 2 with Y with revisions 1 to 2, and asserts XaY; a second case with revisions 1 to 2 then 5 to 6 is Revision { line: 1 }; a line whose old text is wrong is Mismatch { line: 0 }. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.
